notes: This fixed benchmark is a current-data regression suite with balanced known-positive, known-negative, and context-specific controls. It tests whether the system preserves established evidence patterns and scientific safeguards using current evidence; it is not retrospective discovery validation. True retrospective cases require frozen or date-bounded evidence snapshots, and prospective claims require preregistered hypotheses evaluated against later evidence.

expectations.rationale: The EGFR positive control requires current TCGA/cBioPortal GBM genomic evidence.
EGFR should retain a non-trivial somatic mutation signal in the current TCGA GBM profile.
An established GBM driver should not collapse into a low-priority negative-control range when the current evidence stack is available.
An established GBM driver should retain at least moderate aggregate evidence confidence.
The PTEN positive control requires current TCGA/cBioPortal evidence.
PTEN should preserve a substantial current GBM mutation signal.
The integrated profile should preserve meaningful GBM relevance for PTEN without requiring every evidence layer to agree.
The current PTEN evidence stack should remain at least moderately supported.
The CDK4 functional positive control requires current DepMap evidence.
CDK4 should preserve a meaningful loss-of-function dependency signal in the strict GBM model set.
CDK4 should not be collapsed into the pan-essential safeguard category.
The integrated profile should retain meaningful research priority while still allowing other dimensions to temper the functional signal.
The RPL3 negative control requires current DepMap evidence.
RPL3 provides a pan-essential control for distinguishing generic cellular essentiality from GBM-specific dependency.
Strong generic dependency alone must not create a high GBM target-priority score.
Pan-essential behavior should reduce disease-specific model relevance.
The HBB negative control requires current functional-screen retrieval so absence of a GBM dependency is evaluated rather than assumed.
HBB should not display a strong current GBM loss-of-function dependency signal.
A non-GBM control should remain below the established-driver range in the integrated target-priority score.
The ALB negative control requires current functional-screen retrieval.
ALB should not display a strong current GBM loss-of-function dependency signal.
A non-GBM control should remain outside the higher-priority range despite broad contextual data availability.
The context case requires preservation of EGFR's current GBM genomic signal.
EGFR should not be mislabeled pan-essential in the current strict GBM panel.
Current DepMap evidence does not support a GBM-selective EGFR dependency, and the system must preserve that discordance instead of forcing agreement.
The current EGFR functional evidence is primarily conventional-cell-line evidence and must retain its limited model-relevance grade.
The context case requires preservation of CDK4's strong functional dependency signal.
The dependency should remain distinguishable from generic pan-essential behavior.
A strong dependency in predominantly conventional models must not be presented as high physiologic model relevance.
Evidence confidence and model relevance are distinct concepts; moderate confidence can coexist with limited model relevance.
The PTEN context case requires preservation of the current genomic alteration signal.
Current strict-GBM DepMap data do not show a loss-of-function dependency for PTEN, so genomic relevance must not be conflated with dependency.
The functional-model context must remain explicitly qualified.
The integrated score should preserve meaningful target context even when functional evidence does not point in the same direction.
